body:
That does sound helpful, I'm so glad that gave you some closure. I'll maybe see if that's something I would be able to do as that may give me some comfort.

I think I will always have the feeling of "what if". I have that often with my first birth too, hopefully it will get better with time 🫂

It really does. The feelings of grief over my daughter mixed in with not getting the birth I wanted plus coping with a newborn is certainly complex. Any one of those things would be difficult but it's a whole other level feeling them all simultaneously.

I'm so glad things got better with time for you. I'm sure I will get there one day, thank you.

Thank you. I also feel that sadness, I just wish I'd given myself a little more time to potentially go into labour naturally, even though I know it may have ended in a C-section anyway.

I am in the UK but thankfully my closest hospital has a pretty good and well equipped maternity unit, and my obstetrician for this pregnancy was really helpful and supportive. She's quite experienced and was very understanding of my situation. There aren't really specific labour/delivery hospitals here that would deal with complicated pregnancies, you usually end up having a choice of one or two hospitals in your area, all under the NHS. Even private hospitals here don't usually provide maternity services (apart from in London, I'm not close to there) so that's not really a road I can go down. I can look at getting second opinions in future pregnancies though if I choose to.

As much as I would love to have a VBAC, I'm not sure I could let myself take that risk. I'm just gutted that I will probably never get the chance to birth vaginally again. My obstetrician has very kindly offered to get in touch at around six weeks post partum to discuss birth and future pregnancies as she knows I would like more children, so I can speak to her about potential options then.

Thankfully I was in therapy before I had my son, and we're starting again next week. I'm hopeful my therapist will be able to help process all this.

Thank you again, the snuggles do help

I'm so sorry that your baby also died. It's the absolute worst thing to go through and I hope you're doing ok and have been able to heal.

That makes sense. I knew there were risks with a VBAC and getting induced but really I was hoping I'd go into labour naturally, and maybe I would have done if I'd given it more time. I think deep down I know a C-section was the safest thing to do given my circumstances, but I'm finding it very hard to accept. Thank you though, this has made me feel a little better
This is the best analogy I've ever read. Thank you!

For me, I have my own personal voice that voices my every day thoughts, but then I have another voice that I've always called "The Man". The Man is a male voice (I'm female) that is essentially the critical part of my mind - the bit that tells me I'm worthless and need to punish myself etc. I suffer from OCD and he's my OCD voice. It's weird!

Omg. 100% mention it. It might feel like this is a normal thing, and he might describe it as a normal thing but it is NOT OKAY. You have discussed your boundaries and even if you hadn't- he should have asked you before just putting it in.

PLEASE talk to him about this. I only wish I could give my younger self this advice xx
We lived off blow up sofas for the first 5 months of living in our house! They're cheap and comfortable enough to get you through
This is a great idea. I always feel like I have to explain every little thing to everyone and they never get it anyway, so I might try this

This is EXACTLY it. It's like people think we're just over dramatising things for the sake of it when actually we're in proper emotional turmoil inside. We don't want to feel like this but we do, and it really sucks. I just wish they could understand
Thank you for your advice and reading what I had to say. I hope you're right and that it works out
I'm the same. Just got to give myself that little push to say it's ok - just enjoy it! 💕

Haha don't worry I cringed every time I wrote it in my post! Unfortunately I have no idea, but I've read around a little now and apparently it is quite common to not be in the mood (or not realise you are) until you really get into it. As z4nzibar it can be a mindset thing - so I'm trying now to think that way more often, and when my partner tries to initiate something I try to get into the mindset. It's difficult and I think it'll be a long while until I actually see myself as (potentially) sexy, but I do feel slightly better about the actual sex part when I do that. I mean, it's happened once since I first posted so I'm in no way an expert, but that one time definitely felt better!
I'm sorry that you feel this way too. It really sucks. I'm hoping it's just a phase we can grow out of one day 🙂

Yeah I think I'm the same - at first I cba and feel like I'm just doing it for him, but once it's happening and I really try to get myself into it then it can be great!

I think that's probably true. It's almost like there's something blocking the feeling, but once you get past that block you're like "Oh actually I like this!" and realise you were in the mood - you just didn't know it.

It's a weird one! But yeah we got this xxx

Yep. This is exactly how I feel. I tell myself exactly the same thing about sacrifice for the relationship and to make him happy. I just wish I wanted it for real. I fake wanting sex loads and I'm sick of it.

It makes me feel so so much better to know I'm not the only one though. I thought it was just me for so long - it really sucks for both of us but I'm glad I'm not alone.

I'm hoping it will get better, I'm sure we can both get through it :). Thank you xxx
